notes: SPRINT-23 adoption, full scope in one sprint (docs/LANGUAGES.md Swift section): all eleven passes enabled -- the NINTH full-scope pack, wave-3 continues. The pinned alex-pinkus/tree-sitter-swift 0.7.1-with-generated-files grammar (the CANONICAL Swift grammar: the tree-sitter org's tree-sitter-swift is an abandoned unrelated project whose own README redirects here, and every npm tree-sitter-swift version publishes from alex-pinkus; the tag carries NO v prefix) is byte-verified against the npm binding package tree-sitter-swift@0.7.1 for parser.c/scanner.c/node-types.json/grammar.json/LICENSE. LANGUAGE_VERSION 14, accepted by the vendored runtime (ABI window 13..15). The external scanner (src/scanner.c: block comments, raw string parts, implicit/explicit semicolons, the &&/||/?? operator tokens, the #if directive tokens) is picked up by oc_add_grammar automatically. Symbols: function_declaration WITH its function_body field -- free functions, methods, extension methods (the receiver is the extension declaration, not part of the function), static/class methods, nested and generic functions; init_declaration/deinit_declaration with a body ARE symbols named init/deinit (the C# constructor precedent; the grammar gives init no readable name node so the C side synthesizes the spellings); a protocol_function_declaration WITH a default body is a symbol (the pinned grammar wraps the default body in a nested protocol_function_declaration node -- the C# interface-default precedent, a body carries decisions that would otherwise count toward nothing); body-less protocol REQUIREMENTS are NOT symbols (the C prototype discipline). Lambdas (lambda_literal) are anonymous constructs: NOT symbols, decisions count inward. Property accessor bodies ARE symbols (the C# SPRINT-14 accounting-hole precedent): computed_getter/computed_setter AND the implicit getter (statements directly in the computed_property) surface as Prop.get/Prop.set, the observers as Prop.willSet/Prop.didSet -- the owner is a PARENT CLIMB (the accessors nest INSIDE the property_declaration, unlike Kotlin's sibling walk); an accessor with no statements (an empty didSet {}) never matches. Parameters: the parameter node HAS fields -- name = the name field (an external argument label rides external_name and stays out of the name), type = the named child after the ':' token (the generated parser labels the TYPE with the name field too -- a quirk the probe caught; the extraction is positional), default = the default_value field INSIDE the node; a trailing anonymous '...' child collapses the variadic to the '...' marker (the C++ convention). Decision table: if_statement (else-if nested), guard_statement, ternary_expression (the C# conditional_expression precedent), switch_entry (EVERY arm counts including the default arm -- the Rust match_arm discipline), for_statement, while_statement, repeat_while_statement (Swift's do-while), catch_block, nil_coalescing_expression (the C# '??' op precedent as its own node kind -- the Kotlin elvis_expression precedent) and the two boolean containers conjunction_expression/disjunction_expression (Swift has NO shared binary_expression; as kinds each named node counts once per occurrence -- identical semantics). '#if' compilation directives are NOT a decision kind (the C/C++/C# packs count no preprocessor conditional). Resolver v1-swift: the DECLARED-FACT resolver, the MODULE spelling -- Swift's import specifier names a compilation TARGET, a fact no source file carries, so resolution keys on the MANIFEST-declared facts: every analyzed Package.swift contributes (target name, declared path) pairs through the target-hint channel (the manifest filename is SPM's own fixed convention, not a heuristic; the extraction reads the .target/.executableTarget/.testTarget calls' name: and path: string literals, nothing else); each analyzed file joins its module by the DECLARED path (an explicit path: as written, else the SPM documented default Sources/<name> -- the same class of build-system rule as the javac package==directory mapping); files outside every declared target stay module-less and are never import targets. Import shapes: 'M' (whole-module), 'M.Sub' (submodule -- the FIRST segment is the module, the refine is a recorded v1 boundary) and kind-scoped 'import kind M.T' bind the LAST segment as a named member claim (the over-mark direction bounded by the declared facts); everything else binds NULL = the wholesale fail-open claim (importing a module loads all of it, the Kotlin wildcard discipline). The pinned grammar has NO import-alias shape (probed boundary: 'import struct Kit.Tag as T' does not parse -- recorded, never guessed). Without hints every specifier stays unresolved (the honest degradation). The imports relation is a SET. OC005 marking: NULL-bind claims mark whole files (fail-open); kind-scoped member claims mark the matching export. Entry points: EMPTY manifest list BY DESIGN -- the entry claim is the PARSE FACT of top-level code (the Q_SW_TOP fact: Swift's spec lets exactly one file per module carry top-level statements -- the C# 9 global-statement precedent; a top-level let is a DECLARATION and never fires it). Test conventions: none registered in v1 (no runner-executed Swift convention is name-pinned). OC007 fires with a Cobertura-shaped XML via --coverage. Supply tier (the honest delineation): the Swift pack has NO canonical dependency manifest reader in v1 -- Package.resolved IS a version-pinned artifact but no OSV Swift ecosystem exists and none is invented, so OC009/OC010 are enabled pack data that never discover anything: the SWIFT pack contributes zero manifest rows on any scan; on a Swift-only scan the supply block is ABSENT (on a mixed scan the block may carry the OTHER packs' tiers while the Swift contribution stays zero). Metaprogramming (macros, property wrappers, result builders, #if evaluation) is a parse fact only as far as the grammar sees it -- the Rust macro boundary, accepted in the over-report direction for OC006. As-written analysis: no build-system evaluation beyond the manifest's declared target table; swift-tools-version gating is not evaluated. The pinned grammar's known boundaries (measured and classified at the corpus gate): import aliases do not parse ('import struct Kit.Tag as T'); newer Swift syntax (macros, if/switch expressions) may fall to error nodes and is reported honestly as parse errors.
